findings.summary: `externalIdPayload` accepts a merge-group `checkSha` unrelated to `headSha`; the policy requires it be head-derived, but the runtime schema and regression test only require its presence. A forged or erroneous persisted payload can therefore bind the published external ID to a different check SHA without schema rejection.

Merge-group `pullRequests` is only constrained to unique positive integers. It does not enforce the policy-required numeric-ascending order derived from canonical component keys, so multiple external-ID payload encodings can represent the same component set and break the claimed canonical binding.

`fileRecord.previousPath` for renamed files permits traversal-like and otherwise unsafe paths (for example `../x`), unlike manifest file keys. This leaves the old-side canonical diff/path handling outside the closed runtime contract.
